column1: # Fixture rep table for the session walk (bead tla-1sh7.11).
# WHY THIS IS A SECOND TABLE RATHER THAN ROWS ADDED TO REPS.tsv. The four reps
# in REPS.tsv are pinned by name all through harness/test-recall-runner.sh:
# part 1 grades every CASE row over them, part 9 counts the six-field and
# seven-field rows, and part 11 pins two block lengths to the line. Rows added
# there would move numbers that have nothing to do with a session. This table
# is read by part 14 and by nothing else.
# WHAT IT IS SHAPED FOR, which is the ordering rather than the grading. The
# walk draws the next rep from the constructs NEAR the one just served, so a
# table has to carry enough distinct constructs for "near" to mean something.
# Eight constructs at two reps each is the smallest table where a window of
# two reaches 2 of the 7 other constructs rather than most of them.
# THE ORDER OF THE ROWS IS THE DATA. recall/REPS.tsv is sorted by family, then
# by construct, and the reps for one construct are contiguous. Measured over
# the shipped table on 2026-10-17: 37 constructs in four family runs, core
# then sequences then sets then functions-records, so 33 of the 36 adjacent
# construct pairs are same-family. That is what makes file-order adjacency a
# family proxy, and it is why the walk needs no second file in a delivered
# tree. This fixture is sorted the same way: core, then sets, then
# functions-records.
# Every canonical here evaluates over harness/fixtures/recall/env/shunting.tla,
# which declares Wagons and Tracks and nothing else. They are deliberately
# cheap: part 14 grades a handful of them for real and skips the rest, and a
# canonical whose value enumerates is wall time the ordering rows do not need.
#   1  marker       the literal REP
#   2  id           stable, never renumbered
#   3  construct    K001-K105, resolving to a drill/INVENTORY.md row
#   4  environment  resolves to <env-dir>/<name>.tla
#   5  prompt       English, naming none of the notation it asks for
#   6  canonical    the answer, as TLA+
